questions.questionText: What is an SVM trying to maximize when finding its decision boundary?
options: The margin — the distance between the boundary and the closest points of each class
questions.correctAnswer: The margin — the distance between the boundary and the closest points of each class
questions.explanation: A wide margin makes the boundary more robust to noise and new data; the SVM is specifically the maximum-margin classifier.

questions.questionText: What does the kernel trick let an SVM do?
options: Train faster on any dataset size
Separate classes that aren't linearly separable in the original feature space, without explicitly computing higher-dimensional features
Convert the problem into a decision tree
questions.correctAnswer: Separate classes that aren't linearly separable in the original feature space, without explicitly computing higher-dimensional features
questions.explanation: Kernels implicitly compute what a linear boundary would look like in a higher-dimensional mapped space, letting the SVM handle non-linear boundaries efficiently.

questions.questionText: What does a very large value of the regularization parameter C tend to cause?
options: A wider margin and more tolerance for misclassified points
A narrower margin that fits the training data closely, risking overfitting
The kernel trick to stop working
C has no effect on the margin
questions.correctAnswer: A narrower margin that fits the training data closely, risking overfitting
questions.explanation: Large C heavily penalizes margin violations, pushing the SVM toward a tighter fit around the training data — the same overfitting risk seen with other models' complexity knobs.
